problem: LLM/VLM-based navigation (LM-Nav, BehAV) is weak at spatial reasoning, and diffusion-based local policies (ViNT, NoMaD) are short-range and drift over long outdoor routes. Satellite maps used by ViKiNG are stale, oblique and occluded.
motivation: Long-distance outdoor navigation needs local adaptability, global spatial reasoning and semantic instruction understanding together. In sparse-landmark, visually similar unstructured areas the local planner's short perceptual horizon (<5m) accumulates deviation over >100m routes, so global traversability guidance from a fresh overhead map is needed.
key_idea: Combine a language-driven topological-graph planner (GPT-4o + CLIP + modified Dijkstra), a diffusion local planner that samples 8 candidate trajectories, and a U-Net global planner on UAV orthophotos that scores candidates by traversability probability.
insight: The ablations show that LP-only and GP-only are each clearly worse than LP+GP (structured IC 5.05 and 5.65 vs 1.25; unstructured IC 12.10 and 15.60 vs 4.05), so the local and global planners are complementary. Global traversability re-ranking of diffusion samples is what most reduces manual interventions, particularly in unstructured scenes with similar-looking landmarks. The evidence is small-scale, with a single route per environment and 20 trials.
method: Landmark extraction: GPT-4o with a designed prompt parses the instruction into an ordered landmark list.
Visual-semantic matching: CLIP similarity between each topology-graph node's first-person images and the landmark texts gives matrix S (max over images).
Path generation: improved Dijkstra with node value Q(v)=sum_j S_{v,j} - beta*D(start,v) balances semantics and path cost to produce the node path.
Local planner: DDPM conditioned on the visual observation, subgoal image and localization coordinates; 50 denoising steps produce 8 candidate trajectories.
Global planner: U-Net on UAV digital orthophoto maps outputs a pixel traversability probability map; candidates are scored as sum of P_m*P_w over N waypoints, and the best is selected.
GP training: focal-style loss -lambda(1-p)^gamma log p with lambda=3, gamma=2, learned from trajectory data.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) + CLIP (frozen) + DDPM diffusion local planner + U-Net/MLP global planner (trained)
setting.training_data: Data collected in the two test parks (trajectory data for the GP, datasets per environment for the LP); scale not given
setting.observation: monocular RGB camera + GPS, plus UAV orthophoto (DOM) global map
setting.action_space: predicted local trajectories (waypoints) selected from 8 diffusion samples
setting.privileged: UAV orthophoto map of the test area (prior aerial mapping) and a pre-built topology graph of the environment

numbers_note: Only custom real-world metrics on two self-built routes; no standard VLN benchmark. Table cell values are printed with different decimals (e.g. 12.10 as 12.10).
results: KiteRunner cuts interventions to 1.25 (structured) and 4.05 (unstructured), versus 6.10 and 15.05 for the best baseline NoMaD. Path efficiency improves 5.6% and 12.8% over NoMaD (1.07 to 1.01; 1.17 to 1.02), and execution time drops to 598.12 s and 650.35 s from 628.47 s and 792.56 s for NoMaD.
limitations: Evaluation is on only two routes in two parks, 20 trials each, with baselines (ViNT, GNM, NoMaD) augmented with the authors' own language module, so the comparison may not be fully fair.
Requires prior UAV orthophoto and a pre-built topology graph, and the UAV is not used in real time during the run, which limits real-time adaptation.
The paper does not evaluate on standard VLN benchmarks or report success rate; details of training data and hyperparameters (beta, P_w) are missing.
